entry.title: NPR Music: Kokoroko: Tiny Desk Concert
entry.summary:
Kokoroko: Tiny Desk Concert
Onome Edgeworth, Kokoroko’s percussionist and band leader, admits she was bricking it before stepping up to the Tiny Desk—“No chance. This is going to go horribly wrong,” she confessed. But those nerves vanished as soon as the NPR crowd showered them with “good vibes.” This young British crew proved they’ve got the chops to back up the hype, turning initial jitters into a joyous, tight-knit performance. Their set pulls from the new album Tuff Times Never Last, a timely record that tackles life’s rough patches while on a mission to choose joy. Tracks like “Never Lost,” “Together We Are” and “Idea 5 (Call My Name)” highlight a bold leap in both individual and harmonic vocals, and the band’s blend of funk, jazz, afrobeats and R&B creates a refreshingly singular experience—capping it all off with the sweet groove of “Sweetie.” Watch on YouTube

entry.title: NPR Music: Tyshawn Sorey’s powerful sounds of silence | Amplify with Lara Downes
entry.summary: Tyshawn Sorey’s Monochromatic Light (Afterlife) drew its power from the Rothko Chapel’s shadowy stillness and Morton Feldman’s score, inviting listeners into a world where darkness reveals subtle shifts of light and time. At NPR’s makeshift recording studio in an abandoned depot during the Big Ears Festival, Sorey explained how space and silence become active forces in his work—much like Rothko’s near-black canvases that transform as sunlight drifts through the chapel’s skylight. Moving effortlessly between drum kit, trombone, piano and orchestral scores, Sorey embraces both improvisation and notation to let textures and pauses speak louder than notes. Bass-baritone Davóne Tines, who performs in the piece, calls those silences “places of reflection and rest,” a counterweight to our fast-paced world and a reminder that sometimes the most powerful sounds are the ones we almost don’t hear. Watch on YouTube

entry.title: 8-Bit Music Theory: How to Write Gorgeous Chords like Masashi Hamauzu
entry.summary:
How to Write Gorgeous Chords like Masashi Hamauzu
Masashi Hamauzu’s signature sound comes from a clever twist on sus chords—dubbed the “Sus Chord Slash Chord”—that gives his harmonies a lush, colorful vibe. In this tutorial you’ll learn what makes these chords tick and why they’re so irresistible in game-music contexts. Along the way you’ll explore the smoky minor 11, dreamy maj 13, shimmering maj7 #11 and that fresh maj2 first-inversion texture, then see how to weave them all together into chords that feel both modern and magically cinematic. entry.title: Researchers find adding this one simple sentence to prompts makes AI models way more creative
entry.summary: One of the coolest things about generative AI models — both large language models (LLMs) and diffusion-based image generators — is that they are "non-deterministic." That is, despite their reputation among some critics as being "fancy autocorrect," generative AI models actually generate their outputs by choosing from a distribution of the most probable next tokens (units of information) to fill out their response. Asking an LLM: "What is the capital of France?" will have it sample its probability distribution for France, capitals, cities, etc. to arrive at the answer "Paris." But that answer could come in the format of "The capital of France is Paris," or simply "Paris" or "Paris, though it was Versailles at one point."
